issue.title: Two-qubit synthesis to ["cx", "rz", "sx", "x"] returns a wrong circuit (1 - F_avg ≈ 0.07) near the two-CX boundary
issue.body:
### Environment Qiskit version: 2.5.2 (latest release on PyPI at the time of writing; reproduced in a fresh virtual environment with numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1, rustworkx 0.18.1) Python version: 3.12.13 Operating system: Linux (WSL2, glibc 2.43) ### What is happening?

Qiskit bug report -- text for each field of the GitHub form

Open https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit/issues/new/choose and choose Bug report. Copy each block below into the field with the same name.

Title

Two-qubit synthesis to ["cx", "rz", "sx", "x"] returns a wrong circuit (1 - F_avg ≈ 0.07) near the two-CX boundary

Environment

  • Qiskit version: 2.5.2 (latest release on PyPI at the time of writing; reproduced in a fresh virtual environment with numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1, rustworkx 0.18.1)
  • Python version: 3.12.13
  • Operating system: Linux (WSL2, glibc 2.43)

What is happening?

For the canonical two-qubit gate exp(i(0.6 XX + 0.3 YY + c ZZ)) with c = 3e-8, 1e-7 and 3e-7, TwoQubitBasisDecomposer(CXGate(), euler_basis="ZSX") returns a circuit whose unitary differs from the input with average gate infidelity 6.99e-2. The circuit has 3 CX gates, so the error is not visible from the gate counts.

The same failure appears in plain transpile() of a UnitaryGate to basis_gates=["cx", "rz", "sx", "x"], at every optimization level (0-3): 3 CX at levels 0-1 and 2 CX at levels 2-3, with the same infidelity. It also appears when the core is dressed with fixed single-qubit layers on both sides.

Not affected in our tests:

  • the same decomposer with its default Euler basis (TwoQubitBasisDecomposer(CXGate())): exact on the same inputs;
  • a CZ basis (["cz", "rz", "sx", "x"]), levels 1 and 3;
  • a two-qubit GenericBackendV2 target with error data, levels 1 and 3;
  • the same gate given as RXX/RYY/RZZ instead of a UnitaryGate.

Results are exact at c = 1e-8 (2 CX, within the documented approximation) and from c = 5e-7 upward.

How can we reproduce the issue?

from qiskit import QuantumCircuit, transpile
from qiskit.circuit.library import CXGate, UnitaryGate
from qiskit.quantum_info import Operator, average_gate_fidelity
from qiskit.synthesis import TwoQubitBasisDecomposer

core = QuantumCircuit(2)
core.rxx(-1.2, 0, 1)   # a = 0.6
core.ryy(-0.6, 0, 1)   # b = 0.3
core.rzz(-2e-7, 0, 1)  # c = 1e-7
u = Operator(core)

out = TwoQubitBasisDecomposer(CXGate(), euler_basis="ZSX")(u.data)
print("decomposer ZSX:", 1 - average_gate_fidelity(Operator(out), u))          # ~6.99e-02

out_default = TwoQubitBasisDecomposer(CXGate())(u.data)
print("decomposer default:", 1 - average_gate_fidelity(Operator(out_default), u))  # ~1e-16

qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
qc.append(UnitaryGate(u.data), [0, 1])
for level in range(4):
    t = transpile(qc, basis_gates=["cx", "rz", "sx", "x"], optimization_level=level)
    print("transpile level", level, ":", 1 - average_gate_fidelity(Operator(t), u))  # ~6.99e-02 at every level

Scan over c (1 - F_avg, number of 2-qubit gates), UnitaryGate input:

c | decomposer ZSX | [cx,rz,sx,x] L0 / L1 | [cx,rz,sx,x] L2 / L3 | [cz,rz,sx,x] L1 / L3 -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 1e-8 | 3e-16 (2) | 3e-16 (2) | 3e-16 (2) | 2e-16 (2) 3e-8 | 6.99e-2 (3) | 6.99e-2 (3) | 6.99e-2 (2) | 6e-16 (3) 1e-7 | 6.99e-2 (3) | 6.99e-2 (3) | 6.99e-2 (2) | 3e-16 (3) 3e-7 | 6.99e-2 (3) | 6.99e-2 (3) | 6.99e-2 (2) | 3e-16 (3) 1e-6 | 6e-16 (3) | 6e-16 (3) | 8e-13 (3 / 2) | 3e-16 (3) 1e-5 | 3e-16 (3) | 3e-16 (3) | 3e-16 (3) | 3e-16 (3)

What should happen?

The synthesized circuit should match the input to within the decomposer's requested fidelity (1 - 1e-9 by default), as it does with the default Euler basis and with a CZ basis.

Any suggestions?

The infidelity is identical (6.987e-2) at every c in the band and with or without single-qubit dressing, which suggests one wrongly taken branch -- perhaps in the ZSX single-qubit synthesis of a local factor near a degenerate angle -- rather than accumulated rounding. This is a guess from the outside; we have not read the source.

For context: we found this while testing a downstream two-qubit synthesizer that delegated its CX-basis step to this decomposer; we now check the decomposer's output and fall back to the default Euler basis when it is off. A larger scan (four families of near-degenerate cores, 272 blocks) found 48 blocks with this 6.99e-2 error and no failures of the default-Euler decomposer.

comments.body: Disclosure, per the contributing guidelines: I drafted the text of this report with the help of an AI assistant. I ran every reproduction myself (Qiskit 2.5.2, in a fresh virtual environment as well as my working one), and every number in the report comes from those runs. The short script under "How can we reproduce the issue?" is the quickest way to check it. I'm happy to run anything else that would help narrow it down.

comments.body: I’d like to work on this issue. I’ll investigate the ZSX decomposition near the 2-CX/3-CX boundary and add a regression test to ensure the synthesized circuit matches the input unitary within the required fidelity.
comments.author: rupasri118

comments.body:
Thanks for this report.  This does seem to be a real issue, and a serious error in compilation (though gates close to but not _on_ the 2-cx boundary are probably/hopefully rare; certainly they're rare in things like drawing from the Haar measure).  @ShellyGarion: when you're back from holiday, can you look into this?

It may well be the case that there's a typo in the code made during the translation from Python to Rust, and it's a problem that our test suite didn't catch it.

comments.body:
Follow-up: the same failure through transpile(..., backend=<cx device>) at optimization levels 1 and 3

A correction to my original report first: I wrote that a backend with error data did not show the failure. That backend was a cz backend (GenericBackendV2 with cz, rz, sx, x). With a cx device Target the failure does occur, through a plain transpile(qc, backend=..., optimization_level=3).

Environment: qiskit 2.5.2 (latest on PyPI), qiskit-ibm-runtime 0.49.0, Python 3.12.13, Linux (WSL2).

Input: the fixed dressed core of the original reproduction, u(PRE) · exp(i(0.6 XX + 0.3 YY + c ZZ)) · u(POST), as one UnitaryGate on qubits [0, 1]. The compiled circuit is checked on its active physical qubits with the initial and final layout taken into account (1 − process fidelity, global phase ignored).

c | FakeAuckland L1 | FakeAuckland L3 | FakeHanoiV2 L1 | FakeHanoiV2 L3 | FakeTorino L1 | FakeTorino L3 -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 1e-8 | 2.2e-16 (2 CX) | 2.2e-16 (2) | 2.2e-16 (2) | 2.2e-16 (2) | 0 (2 CZ) | 0 (2) 3e-8 | 8.7e-2 (3) | 8.7e-2 (2) | 8.7e-2 (3) | 8.7e-2 (2) | 2.2e-16 (3) | 0 (3) 1e-7 | 8.7e-2 (3) | 8.7e-2 (2) | 8.7e-2 (3) | 8.7e-2 (2) | 0 (3) | 0 (3) 3e-7 | 8.7e-2 (3) | 8.7e-2 (2) | 8.7e-2 (3) | 8.7e-2 (2) | 0 (3) | 0 (3) 1e-6 | 6.7e-16 (3) | 1.0e-12 (2) | 6.7e-16 (3) | 1.0e-12 (2) | 0 (3) | 4.4e-16 (3) 1e-5 | 6.7e-16 (3) | 0 (3) | 6.7e-16 (3) | 6.7e-16 (3) | 0 (3) | 0 (3)

How this fits the analysis above:

  • 1 − process fidelity 8.7e-2 is 1 − F_avg = 0.069866, exactly the value of a missing Rz(0.6) on one qubit.
  • 20 random single-qubit dressings of the same core at c = 1e-7 (seeded): 20 of 20 wrong on FakeAuckland and FakeHanoiV2 at both levels, all at the same value; FakeTorino 0 of 20. The error is set by the core, not by the dressing, as expected if rz(θ1) of the middle unitary is dropped.
  • In a larger test with random cores (near-boundary unitaries in 4- and 6-qubit circuits), level 3 with the FakeAuckland, FakeHanoiV2, FakeAlgiers and FakeGeneva Targets returned a wrong circuit for 28 of 40 circuits on each device, with output-state infidelity up to 0.34. That test passed approximation_degree=1.0 explicitly. This range is consistent with the θ1-dependence above (worst seen 0.36). The cz devices (FakeTorino, FakeKingston) were exact.

Why this matters: users who compile explicit two-qubit unitaries (for example from numerical optimisation) for cx devices with the default preset pipeline get a silently wrong circuit. At level 3 the wrong circuit is also the shorter one (2 CX instead of 3), so it would be preferred. As far as I can see, the pulse_optimize=False workaround is not reachable through transpile(), so there is no workaround in the default pipeline.

I have not tested the candidate fix on this path.

Reproduction script (Qiskit only):

<details><summary>repro_qiskit_17057_target.py</summary> 
"""repro_qiskit_17057_target.py -- does Qiskit issue #17057 also reach transpile() with a real cx device Target?

repro_qiskit_zsx_2q_v2.py (the reproduction attached to #17057) found wrong circuits from
transpile(basis_gates=[cx, rz, sx, x]) for near-boundary two-qubit unitaries, and none with a cz backend that has
error data. This script asks the open question: what happens with a cx device's Target (FakeAuckland, FakeHanoiV2),
as in `transpile(qc, backend=..., optimization_level=3)`? FakeTorino (cz) is the control.

Input: the same fixed dressed core as repro_qiskit_zsx_2q_v2.py,
    u(PRE) . exp(i(0.6 XX + 0.3 YY + c ZZ)) . u(POST),  c in 1e-8 .. 1e-5,
given as one UnitaryGate on qubits [0, 1]; plus 20 random dressings at c = 1e-7 (seeded).

Check: the compiled circuit's operator on its active physical qubits is restricted to the input subspace (logical
qubits at the initial layout, every other active qubit in |0>) and output subspace (final layout, others in |0>);
reported is 1 - process fidelity against the input unitary (global phase ignored), plus any leakage. Nothing here
uses PSF-Zero.
Usage:
    python -u repro_qiskit_17057_target.py 2>&1 | tee repro_qiskit_17057_target.txt
"""
import itertools
import platform

import numpy as np
import qiskit
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit, transpile
from qiskit.circuit.library import UnitaryGate
from qiskit.quantum_info import Operator, random_unitary

A, B = 0.6, 0.3
CS = [1e-8, 3e-8, 1e-7, 3e-7, 1e-6, 1e-5]
PRE = [(0.7, 0.2, -1.1), (1.9, -0.4, 0.3)]
POST = [(2.3, 1.0, 0.5), (0.4, -2.2, 1.7)]
WRONG = 1e-6


def dressed(c, pre=None, post=None):
    """The fixed dressed core (or a dressing given as 2x2 unitaries) as a 4x4 matrix, wrapped in a UnitaryGate."""
    core = QuantumCircuit(2)
    core.rxx(-2 * A, 0, 1)
    core.ryy(-2 * B, 0, 1)
    core.rzz(-2 * c, 0, 1)
    qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
    for q in range(2):
        if pre is None:
            qc.u(*PRE[q], q)
        else:
            qc.append(UnitaryGate(pre[q]), [q])
    qc.compose(core, inplace=True)
    for q in range(2):
        if post is None:
            qc.u(*POST[q], q)
        else:
            qc.append(UnitaryGate(post[q]), [q])
    u = Operator(qc).data
    out = QuantumCircuit(2)
    out.append(UnitaryGate(u), [0, 1])
    return out, u


def logical_error(tqc, u):
    """(1 - process fidelity, leakage) of the compiled circuit against the 4x4 unitary u."""
    active = sorted({tqc.find_bit(q).index for ins in tqc.data for q in ins.qubits
                     if ins.operation.name not in ("barrier", "delay", "measure")})
    lay = tqc.layout
    init = list(lay.initial_index_layout(filter_ancillas=True)[:2])
    fin = list(lay.final_index_layout(filter_ancillas=True)[:2])
    active = sorted(set(active) | set(init) | set(fin))
    pos = {p: j for j, p in enumerate(active)}
    red = QuantumCircuit(len(active), global_phase=tqc.global_phase)
    for ins in tqc.data:
        if ins.operation.name in ("barrier", "delay", "measure"):
            continue
        red.append(ins.operation, [pos[tqc.find_bit(q).index] for q in ins.qubits])
    v = Operator(red).data
    m = len(active)

    def index(bits_at):  # little-endian basis index with the given active qubits set
        return sum(1 << pos[p] for p, b in bits_at if b)

    blk = np.zeros((4, 4), dtype=complex)
    for i, (b0, b1) in enumerate(itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=2)):
        col = index([(init[0], b0), (init[1], b1)])
        for j, (c0, c1) in enumerate(itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=2)):
            row = index([(fin[0], c0), (fin[1], c1)])
            # Qiskit little-endian: logical index = bit(q0) + 2 bit(q1)
            blk[c0 + 2 * c1, b0 + 2 * b1] = v[row, col]
    leak = float(1 - np.linalg.norm(blk, "fro") ** 2 / 4)
    fid = abs(np.trace(u.conj().T @ blk) / 4) ** 2
    return float(1 - fid), leak, m


def main():
    from qiskit_ibm_runtime import fake_provider
    import qiskit_ibm_runtime
    print(f"qiskit {qiskit.__version__} | qiskit-ibm-runtime {qiskit_ibm_runtime.__version__} | "
          f"python {platform.python_version()} | {platform.platform()}")
    backends = [fake_provider.FakeAuckland(), fake_provider.FakeHanoiV2(), fake_provider.FakeTorino()]
    cells = [(b, lvl) for b in backends for lvl in (1, 3)]
    head = " | ".join(f"{b.name[:13]:>13s} L{lvl}" for b, lvl in cells)
    print(f"\n--- fixed dressed core, 1 - process fidelity (cx count) ---\n{'c':>7s} | {head}")
    bad = []
    for c in CS:
        qc, u = dressed(c)
        row = []
        for b, lvl in cells:
            tqc = transpile(qc, backend=b, optimization_level=lvl, seed_transpiler=0)
            err, leak, _ = logical_error(tqc, u)
            n2 = sum(1 for ins in tqc.data if len(ins.qubits) == 2)
            row.append(f"{err:9.1e} ({n2})")
            if err > WRONG or leak > WRONG:
                bad.append((c, b.name, lvl, err))
        print(f"{c:7.0e} | " + " | ".join(f"{x:>16s}" for x in row))

    print("\n--- 20 random dressings at c = 1e-7: circuits with 1 - F > 1e-6 (max) ---")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(17057)
    seeds = [[int(s) for s in rng.integers(2**31, size=4)] for _ in range(20)]
    for b, lvl in cells:
        errs = []
        for s in seeds:
            qc, u = dressed(1e-7, pre=[random_unitary(2, seed=s[0]).data, random_unitary(2, seed=s[1]).data],
                            post=[random_unitary(2, seed=s[2]).data, random_unitary(2, seed=s[3]).data])
            tqc = transpile(qc, backend=b, optimization_level=lvl, seed_transpiler=0)
            errs.append(logical_error(tqc, u)[0])
        print(f"  {b.name:14s} L{lvl}: {sum(e > WRONG for e in errs):2d} of 20 wrong (max {max(errs):.1e})")

    print("\nwrong (fixed core):", bad if bad else "none")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
</details>

As before: I used an AI assistant for analysis and drafting; all numbers were run and checked locally.
